conventions.convention: Positions x are dimensionless and represent physical positions ℓ₀x; E₀ = 1 J, numerical energy is H/E₀, and numerical inverse temperature is E₀β. Density and energy density per physical d-volume acquire a factor ℓ₀⁻ᵈ.

Configurations are unordered simple sets. The exact-N positional reference is the quotient push-forward of completed product Lebesgue measure divided by N!, with vacuum mass one. The normalized Poisson reference is QΛ = exp(−|Λ|) ΣN μΛ,N.
Periodic energy uses the complete image sum, omitting only the identical point and including a particle's nontrivial self-images; the ordered image sum has factor 1/2.

Positive-temperature canonical and grand laws assign zero weight to infinite-energy configurations and are adopted preparations, without a dynamical equilibration or empirical thermalization conclusion.

The exact-N shell is a uniform positional energy-density window with positive finite reference measure; its shrinking width is selected by a theorem, not prescribed arbitrarily. It contains no kinetic energy or exact-energy surface measure.
At β = 0, hard exclusions remain as an admissibility indicator, including forbidden periodic-image pairs; the expression 0·(+∞) is never evaluated.
Stationary-law restrictions and relative entropy use the uncompleted bounded-Borel count sigma-algebra, not an assumed extension of arbitrary stationary laws to the completed positional quotient.
A supporting activity satisfies F(s,β)+αs ≤ F(ρ,β)+αρ, with z = exp(α). Local expectations concern periodic continuation of torus preparations.
Van Hove regions satisfy the two-sided Euclidean fixed-width boundary-layer condition. The exterior class Ω(t) has one fixed centered-cell square-count bound for every integer box size.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the positional pair model, numerical-to-SI conversion, stability, decreasing integrable tail, and complete periodic image energy. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses.
Adopts μΛ,N = (1/N!)(qN)#λΛ⊗N on simple unordered positional configurations, vacuum mass one, and QΛ = exp(−|Λ|) ΣN μΛ,N.
Adopts normalized finite-volume canonical and grand positional weights on finite-energy configurations, and the controlled shell law only when its shell has positive finite reference measure.

At the selected parameter point, adopts a singleton stationary finite-intensity minimizer of I+βΦ−ρ log z on the positive-beta finite-entropy, finite-energy domain, or of I−ρ log z on the retained hard-admissible zero-beta domain.
Under AC, d ≥ 2, a stable regularly tempered Borel numerical pair potential, and the adopted positive-temperature grand preparation, pL = kBT log ΞL/(ℓ₀ᵈ|ΛL|) has a finite free-cube limit.

Under AC and superstable regular Borel pair hypotheses, free-wall grand pressure and positive-interior-density exact-N canonical rates have their cube limits on van Hove regions. With the additional stated finite-valued divergent positive core, exterior grand pressure converges uniformly for each fixed Ω(t).

concerns.concern: F1 verifies the mathematical supplier's maximum-norm far-tail condition but does not explicitly verify its lower-regularity condition near the origin. The physical definition assumes stability plus a far tail, whereas def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction defines regularity using an integrable lower envelope on all radii. A reader can close this: two-particle stability gives φ(x) ≥ −2B for nonzero x, so extend the tail envelope by a sufficiently large constant on the bounded near region, also covering φ(0) if necessary.

F1 supplies the far-tail norm conversion but leaves the same near-origin lower-regularity bridge unstated before invoking the stable regular mathematical carriers. Two-particle stability and a constant extension of the decreasing tail envelope supply the missing verification.

alerts.finding: Proof step 1.1 says: “it has a finite supporting slope α at ρ. Put z=e^α>0.” For a concave canonical rate with supporting slope s, the displayed duality P(α,β)=supρ(Fβ(ρ)+αρ) requires α=−s. Indeed, Fβ(r)≤Fβ(ρ)+s(r−ρ) yields maximization of Fβ(r)−sr, not Fβ(r)+sr. The Statement's supporting-activity formulation can remain sound, but this proof sentence has the slope/activity sign reversed. The physical consumer pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local-limit correctly states the supporting inequality explicitly.
